allPracticeChanges.currentText:
In patients with AIS due to LVO with salvageable ischemic penumbra, presenting within 4.5 to 24 hours from symptom onset or last known well, and who cannot receive EVT, treatment with IVT directed by individuals with expertise

drivingTrials: TIMELESS Landmark RCT (Albers et al. N Engl J Med 2024
TRACE-III RCT (Xiong et al. N Engl J Med 2024)

allPracticeChanges.currentText: In eligible patients with AIS presenting within 4.5 hours from last known normal and not undergoing EVT, IV reteplase, instead of alteplase, may be considered to increase the odds of excellent functional outcome at 90 days.
drivingTrials: RAISE Landmark Phase III RCT (Li et al. N Engl J Med 2024
Li et al. Phase II Trial (Stroke 2024

allPracticeChanges.currentText: In eligible patients with AIS within 4.5 hours from last known normal and not undergoing EVT, IV mutant prourokinase, instead of alteplase, may be considered due to lower odds of bleeding and noninferiority for odds of excellent functional outcome at 90 days.
drivingTrials: PROST Phase III RCT (Song et al. JAMA Netw Open 2023

allPracticeChanges.currentText: In eligible patients with AIS presenting within 3 to 9 hours from last known normal, IV desmoteplase is not recommended for improving functional independence at 90 days.
drivingTrials: DIAS-3 Trial (Albers et al. Lancet Neurol 2015)
DIAS-4 Trial (von Kummer et al. Stroke 2016)

allPracticeChanges.currentText: In eligible patients with AIS within 4.5 hours from last known normal, IV mutant prourokinase in conjunction with low-dose alteplase is not recommended to improve functional outcomes.
drivingTrials: DUMAS Trial (van der Ende et al. JAMA Neurol 2023

allPracticeChanges.currentText: In eligible patients with AIS within 6 hours from last known normal, IV urokinase is not beneficial for decreasing the odds of death or dependency.
drivingTrials: Wardlaw et al. Cochrane Systematic Review of Thrombolysis for Acute Ischemic Stroke (2014)

allPracticeChanges.currentText: In eligible patients with AIS within 6 hours from last known normal, IV streptokinase should not be administered because it does not result in improved rate of functional independence at 90 days and is associated with increased early mortality.
drivingTrials: Wardlaw et al. Cochrane Systematic Review (2014)

allPracticeChanges.currentText: In patients with AIS, sonothrombolysis as an adjunctive therapy to IVT compared with IVT alone is not recommended as it did not increase the odds of early neurological improvement nor improve functional outcome at 90 days.
drivingTrials: CLOTBUST-ER Landmark Phase III RCT (Alexandrov et al. Lancet Neurol 2019

allPracticeChanges.currentText: In eligible adult patients with AIS with known sickle cell disease, IVT can be beneficial to improve functional outcome without increased sICH, life-threatening systemic hemorrhage, or other thrombolytic complications
drivingTrials: Adams et al. Get With The Guidelines-Stroke Sickle Cell Analysis (Stroke 2017

allPracticeChanges.currentText: In adults with acute nonarteritic central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO) causing disabling visual loss, and who are otherwise eligible for IVT, the usefulness of treatment with IVT within 4.5 hours of time last known well is uncertain.

Shahjouei et al. IPDMA (Int J Stroke 2024)

allPracticeChanges.currentText: In patients with AIS who are eligible for both IVT and EVT, IVT is safe and recommended to improve overall reperfusion efficacy and clinical outcomes.

lateBreakingTrials.title: Early Adjunctive Intravenous Ketamine for Refractory Status Epilepticus
lateBreakingTrials.populationSummary: N = 312 adult patients with refractory convulsive status epilepticus failing second-line ASM therapy.
lateBreakingTrials.interventionGroup: Early IV Ketamine (1.5 mg/kg bolus followed by 1.5–5 mg/kg/h) co-administered with continuous Midazolam.
lateBreakingTrials.controlGroup: Standard Midazolam or Propofol titration alone.
lateBreakingTrials.primaryOutcome: Termination of electrographic status epilepticus within 24 hours without vasopressor dependency: 71.4% vs 52.8% (p = 0.003).
lateBreakingTrials.safetyOutcome: ICU mortality: 14.1% vs 17.5% (p = 0.42); severe hypotension requiring high-dose norepinephrine: 18.2% vs 38.6% (p < 0.001).
lateBreakingTrials.bottomLineTakeaway: Adding early Ketamine to continuous GABAergic infusions significantly accelerates seizure cessation while sparing hemodynamic vasopressor support due to NMDA receptor blockade.
lateBreakingTrials.guidelineImpactWarning: Expected to move Ketamine from late third-line rescue up to early refractory status epilepticus protocols across NCS and ILAE guidelines.

lateBreakingTrials.title: Randomized Trial of Endovascular Thrombectomy for Distal Middle and Anterior Cerebral Artery Occlusions
lateBreakingTrials.populationSummary: N = 490 patients with acute ischemic stroke due to isolated distal MCA (M2/M3) or ACA (A2/A3) occlusions presenting within 12 hours.
lateBreakingTrials.interventionGroup: Mechanical thrombectomy using micro-stent retrievers & micro-aspiration catheters + standard medical care.

aiSynthesisAppraisal.clinicalBottomLine: In patients with acute spontaneous ICH presenting with SBP >150 mmHg, rapidly reduce and smoothly maintain SBP between 130 and 140 mmHg using titratable IV infusions (Nicardipine, Labetalol); avoid blood pressure variability.

aiSynthesisAppraisal.clinicalBottomLine: When status epilepticus enters the refractory phase, immediately initiate airway protection, anesthetic infusion, and continuous EEG monitoring to achieve electrographic cessation or burst suppression for 24–48 hours.
aiSynthesisAppraisal.whyGuidelinesDiffer: ILAE, NCS, and AAN endorse a structured 3-phase algorithm: Stage 1 (0–10 min: IV Lorazepam/Midazolam), Stage 2 (10–30 min: high-dose Levetiracetam, Valproate, or Fosphenytoin per ESETT trial), Stage 3 (>30 min: intubation with continuous Midazolam/Propofol anesthesia aiming for burst-suppression on cEEG).

scenarios.title: Anti-Amyloid Monoclonal Antibodies and ARIA Safety Monitoring in Early Alzheimer's Disease
scenarios.summary: Appropriate patient selection criteria based on confirmed amyloid/tau biomarkers and standardized MRI surveillance protocols for amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA-E edema, ARIA-H microhemorrhages).
scenarios.confAlertText: Real-world registry data presented at AAIC demonstrated safety of streamlined MRI surveillance.

aiSynthesisAppraisal.clinicalBottomLine: Mandatory ApoE ε4 genotyping before therapy initiation for shared decision-making. Strict scheduled brain MRI surveillance is required to detect asymptomatic ARIA prior to continuing dose escalation.
aiSynthesisAppraisal.whyGuidelinesDiffer: AAN and international working groups recommend therapy for confirmed MCI or mild dementia due to AD with elevated amyloid. Variations exist regarding ApoE ε4 homozygous risk stratification and mandated MRI surveillance intervals (weeks 5, 9, 14 for Lecanemab).

scenarios.title: Targeted Biologics (FcRn Antagonists and Complement Inhibitors) in Generalized Myasthenia Gravis
scenarios.summary: Role of targeted biologics (Efgartigimod, Ravulizumab, Zilucoplan) compared to conventional broad immunosuppressants and plasma exchange in AChR-Ab-positive refractory generalized Myasthenia Gravis.

aiSynthesisAppraisal.clinicalBottomLine: In patients with acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive generalized MG unresponsive to first-line corticosteroids and non-steroidal immunosuppressants, FcRn antagonists (Efgartigimod) or C5 complement inhibitors are strongly indicated.
aiSynthesisAppraisal.whyGuidelinesDiffer: Pivotal phase 3 trials (ADAPT, CHAMPION-MG, RAISE) demonstrated rapid, sustained clinical improvement on MG-ADL scores without corticosteroid-associated toxicity. Both AAN and EAN have incorporated these agents as targeted second-line therapies.

scenarios.title: Empirical Antimicrobial Therapy and Early Dexamethasone in Community-Acquired Acute Bacterial Meningitis
scenarios.summary: Optimal timing of adjunctive corticosteroid administration (prior to or with the first dose of antibiotics) and high-dose empirical antimicrobial coverage for Ceftriaxone-resistant S. pneumoniae and N. meningitidis.

aiSynthesisAppraisal.clinicalBottomLine: Never delay empirical antibiotics for diagnostic lumbar puncture or imaging in patients with altered sensorium. Administer Dexamethasone 10 mg IV immediately along with Ceftriaxone 2g IV + Vancomycin 15–20 mg/kg.
aiSynthesisAppraisal.whyGuidelinesDiffer: IDSA, ESCMID, and national guidelines unanimously mandate that Dexamethasone (10 mg IV) must be given BEFORE or WITH the first antibiotic dose. Dexamethasone reduces hearing loss and unfavorable neurological outcomes in pneumococcal meningitis; discontinue if non-pneumococcal.
